answers.core:
Yes. This kind of functionality is foundational to many genres (strategy, educational, simulation, debugging) and aligns well with Godot’s goal of being a general-purpose, accessible engine.

Reasons to include it in core:

Native nodes benefit from tight integration with UI layout, themes, and drawing systems

Allows consistent cross-platform performance and rendering

Encourages better real-time debugging/telemetry directly in editor tools

Promotes reusability and community adoption for simulations and games

Asset library solutions are often abandoned or fragmented
answers.workaround:
In theory, yes — simple plots can be constructed using Line2D, Control, or Polygon2D, but:

It requires hundreds of lines of boilerplate code for a decent result

Developers must handle axis scaling, labels, colors, padding, tooltips, etc., manually

No standard solution means duplicated work across projects

title: Add a plotting/charting node for data visualization
